mainTopic: Why רבי עקיבא limits היתר מצטרף לאיסור while the רבנן learn טעם כעיקר for the whole Torah, followed by the משנה and שמואל's two versions about dough stuck in the cracks of a kneading bowl.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a discussion from the previous daf. רבי עקיבא learns from נזיר that permitted food joins with forbidden food (היתר מצטרף לאיסור). He does not apply this to the whole Torah, because חטאת teaches the same thing. When two verses teach one idea, no general rule is learned from them (שני כתובין הבאין כאחד אין מלמדין). The רבנן answer that the verses teach different lessons. חטאת teaches היתר מצטרף לאיסור, and the word משרת in נזיר teaches טעם כעיקר, which then applies to the whole Torah. רב אשי asks why, according to רבי עקיבא, a verse is needed to teach that two forbidden foods combine. רב כהנא answers that forbidden and permitted combine only when eaten together, while two forbidden foods combine even when eaten one after the other. A new משנה then rules on dough stuck in the cracks of a kneading bowl, both for removing חמץ and for חציצה when the bowl is immersed. שמואל limits the משנה based on whether the dough strengthens the bowl, and the גמרא gives two versions of his statement, each backed by a ברייתא. The second ברייתא continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Two verses teaching one idea do not spread to the whole Torah
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא does not apply היתר מצטרף לאיסור to all of the Torah, because נזיר and חטאת are two verses that teach the same thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because נזיר and חטאת are two verses that come as one, and such verses do not teach for other cases.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question left open from the previous daf: why does רבי עקיבא limit היתר מצטרף לאיסור and not apply it everywhere? The answer is that the rule shows up in two separate places, נזיר and חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a law in one area can be learned for other areas. But if the Torah bothered to write the same law twice, in two different places, that tells us the law is limited to those cases. If it applied everywhere, one verse would have been enough.

keyTerms.meaning: A nazirite, a person who took a vow that forbids wine and grape products
A sin-offering
Two verses that teach the same idea
They do not teach for other cases

steps.confusionAlert: Two verses here does not mean the idea is twice as strong. It means the idea is limited to just those two cases and is not a general rule.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle is the key reason רבי עקיבא's rule stays limited to נזיר and חטאת. The rest of this passage builds on it.

phrases.english: Because nazirite and sin-offering are
two verses that come as one,
and they do not teach (to other cases).
phrases.notes: A standard rule of Torah interpretation

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוֵה נָזִיר וְחַטָּאת שְׁנֵי כְתוּבִין הַבָּאִין כְּאֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from the previous daf about why רבי עקיבא does not apply היתר מצטרף לאיסור to the whole Torah.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting principle: שני כתובין הבאין כאחד אין מלמדין
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule learned from נזיר should apply to all prohibitions in the Torah.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because the rule appears in both נזיר and חטאת, it stays limited to those two cases.

steps.title: Where does the sin-offering source come from?
steps.stepSummary: The נזיר source was already discussed. The גמרא asks what the source is for the חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Nazirite is what we said. Sin-offering, what is it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to check its claim. We already know the נזיר source, so where in the Torah does חטאת teach the same idea? This sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 1 only works if חטאת really teaches the same law. So the גמרא has to show the text for חטאת. This is a clarifying question, not an attack.

keyTerms.meaning: That which we already said
What is it?

phrases.english: Nazirite is what we said (earlier).
Sin-offering, what is it (the source)?

steps.triggerLanguage: נָזִיר, הָא דַּאֲמַרַן. חַטָּאת מַאי הִיא?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the second verse that step 1 relies on.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source showing that the חטאת also teaches this law.

steps.title: ברייתא: meat is affected only if it absorbs the sin-offering
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא on 'כל אשר יגע בבשרה יקדש' teaches that ordinary meat is affected by the חטאת only if it absorbs its taste.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: 'Anything that touches its flesh shall become holy.' Could it be even if it did not absorb? The verse says 'in its flesh', meaning only once it is absorbed into the flesh.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. The ברייתא first rules that mere touching is not enough. The meat must actually absorb from the חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra word 'בבשרה' (into its flesh) shows that absorption is required. That means taste or absorbed material matters, which is how this verse ties into the laws of mixing.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall become holy (take on the status of the offering)
I might have thought
Therefore the verse says
That it is absorbed

phrases.english: As it was taught (in a baraita):
"Anything that touches its flesh
shall become holy, etc."
Might it be even if it did not absorb?
The verse says: "in its flesh (shall become holy)"
— only once it is absorbed into the flesh.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: כֹּל אֲשֶׁר יִגַּע בִּבְשָׂרָהּ יִקְדָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source asked for in step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The verse 'כל אשר יגע בבשרה יקדש' as explained in a ברייתא.

steps.title: The meat takes on the full status of the sin-offering
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: the absorbing meat becomes exactly like the חטאת. If the חטאת is invalid, the meat is invalid. If it is valid, the meat is eaten under the stricter rules of the חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Shall become holy' means it becomes like it. If the offering is invalid, the meat becomes invalid. If it is valid, the meat is eaten under the stricter rules of the offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes explaining the word 'יקדש'. Ordinary meat that absorbs from a חטאת gets the חטאת's exact status. This completes the חטאת source the גמרא was looking for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the permitted meat is treated as if it were the חטאת itself. That is the idea of היתר מצטרף לאיסור: the permitted food joins the restricted one. Since חטאת teaches this just like נזיר does, we now have two verses for the same law, which confirms step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: To become like it (same status)
Invalid, disqualified
Valid
By the stricter of its rules

steps.whatToRemember: נזיר and חטאת both teach that permitted food joins forbidden food. Because there are two verses, רבי עקיבא does not apply the rule to the rest of the Torah.

phrases.english: "Shall become holy" — to be like it,
so that if it (the offering) is invalid — it becomes invalid,
and if it is valid
— it is eaten by the stricter rules of (the offering).
phrases.notes: Eaten like a חטאת: only by male כהנים, in the Temple area, for a limited time

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא and completes the חטאת source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Meat that absorbs from a חטאת takes on its full status, so חטאת teaches the same law as נזיר.

steps.title: Challenge to the Rabbis: shouldn't their source also be blocked?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: the רבנן learn טעם כעיקר from נזיר. Why not say that נזיר and חטאת are two verses teaching one idea, so it also cannot be applied to the whole Torah?
steps.simpleTranslation: And for the Rabbis too, let nazirite and sin-offering be two verses that come as one, and they should not teach!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the same argument against the רבנן. If two verses block רבי עקיבא, they should also block the רבנן from learning טעם כעיקר for the whole Torah. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא in step 3 showed that חטאת also teaches about absorbed taste ('עד שיבלע'). So for the רבנן, טעם כעיקר seems to appear in both נזיר and חטאת. By the rule from step 1, that should limit it, yet the רבנן apply it everywhere.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages (the majority view against רבי עקיבא)
Also
Let it be
Taste counts like the actual substance (the רבנן's rule; implied, not in this text)

phrases.english: And (according to) the Rabbis also,
let nazirite and sin-offering be
two verses that come as one,
and they should not teach!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן נָמֵי, נִיהְוֵי נָזִיר וְחַטָּאת שְׁנֵי כְתוּבִין הַבָּאִין כְּאֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the principle from step 1 and the חטאת source from steps 3-4 to challenge the רבנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: The רבנן's use of נזיר to teach טעם כעיקר for the whole Torah.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If נזיר and חטאת both teach טעם כעיקר, then the rule of two verses should stop it from spreading to the whole Torah, just as it does for רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: The Rabbis answer that both verses are needed
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן answer the question from step 5. The verses of נזיר and חטאת are both needed, so they are not two verses teaching one idea.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: these two verses are each needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 5 on behalf of the רבנן. Both verses are needed, so the rule of שני כתובים הבאין כאחד does not apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two verses only count as 'teaching one idea' if one of them is extra, meaning it could have been learned from the other. If each verse is needed, neither is extra. Then a general rule can be learned from them.

keyTerms.meaning: These (two verses)
They are each truly needed
Two verses that teach the same thing, so no general rule is learned from them

phrases.english: They say: these are each needed.
phrases.notes: He means the פסוקים about נזיר and about חטאת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 5
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each verse is needed, so they are not 'two verses as one'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: נזיר and חטאת are two verses teaching one idea, so no general rule can be learned
steps.terutzMaskana: Each verse is needed, so a general rule can be learned

steps.title: רבי עקיבא asks why both verses are needed
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא challenges the claim. חטאת could not teach נזיר, but נזיר could teach חטאת, so the חטאת verse is extra.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא would ask: why are both needed? It makes sense that if the Torah had written the rule only for חטאת, we could not learn נזיר from it, because we do not learn ordinary things from holy things. But the Torah could have written it only for נזיר, and then we would learn חטאת from it. After all, all the prohibitions of the Torah are learned from נזיר!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא attacks the רבנן's answer. He shows that one of the two verses was not really needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Learning in one direction fails, because holy things (קדשים) have special strict rules, so they cannot teach ordinary things (חולין). Learning in the other direction works. The רבנן themselves learn every prohibition in the Torah from נזיר, so they could surely learn חטאת from it too. That makes the חטאת verse extra, and the two verses are 'teaching one idea'.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense (granted)
The Merciful One (the Torah)
We do not learn ordinary things from holy things
The prohibitions of the Torah

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva: in what way are they needed?
Granted, if the Merciful One had written it about a sin-offering,
we would not learn nazirite from it —
because we do not learn ordinary things from holy things.
But let the Merciful One write it about a nazirite,
and the sin-offering would come and learn from it,
since, after all, all the prohibitions in the Torah
are learned from nazirite.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תירוץ of step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that both verses are needed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: חטאת can be learned from נזיר, just as the רבנן learn all prohibitions from נזיר. So the חטאת verse is extra, and the two verses are שני כתובים הבאין כאחד.

steps.title: The Rabbis say the two verses teach different lessons
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן answer that חטאת teaches היתר מצטרף לאיסור, which cannot be learned for חולין. The word משרת in נזיר teaches טעם כעיקר, and from there it applies to the whole Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן would tell you: they are truly needed. חטאת teaches that permitted food joins with forbidden food, and ordinary things cannot be learned from holy things. 'משרת' (soaked) teaches that taste counts like the actual food. From here you learn it for the whole Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן defend their view against רבי עקיבא. The two verses are not repeating each other, because each one teaches a different rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חטאת verse teaches היתר מצטרף לאיסור, meaning permitted food joins with forbidden food to make up the required amount. That is a special rule for holy things, which ordinary things cannot learn from. The נזיר word משרת teaches a different rule, טעם כעיקר, meaning taste counts like the actual food. Since the lessons differ, neither verse is extra, and טעם כעיקר spreads to the whole Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: Permitted food joins with forbidden food to make up the amount
'Soaking' (verse about the נזיר and grapes)
The taste counts like the actual substance
From here you learn (a general rule)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two rules. היתר מצטרף לאיסור means permitted food adds up together with forbidden food. טעם כעיקר means the taste alone of forbidden food is enough. The whole disagreement is about which verse teaches which rule.
steps.whatToRemember: For the רבנן, חטאת teaches היתר מצטרף לאיסור and נזיר (משרת) teaches טעם כעיקר. Because the lessons are different, טעם כעיקר applies to the whole Torah.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis would say to you: they are truly needed:
the sin-offering, to teach that permitted joins with forbidden,
and ordinary things are not learned from holy things,
and 'soaked' — to teach that taste is like the substance,

phrases.aramaic: וּמִכָּאן אַתָּה דָּן לְכׇל הַתּוֹרָה כּוּלָּהּ.
phrases.english: and from here you derive for the entire Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי עקיבא's קשיא of step 7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the verses: each one teaches a different rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both verses teach the same thing, so חטאת is extra
steps.terutzMaskana: חטאת teaches היתר מצטרף לאיסור (only for קדשים). משרת teaches טעם כעיקר for the whole Torah.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source of the רבנן's rule that טעם כעיקר applies to all prohibitions in the Torah.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא says both verses teach the same rule
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא holds that both verses teach היתר מצטרף לאיסור. So they are two verses teaching one idea, and they do not teach a general rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא says: both teach that permitted food joins with forbidden food. So they are two verses that teach the same thing, and any two verses that teach the same thing do not teach a general rule.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי עקיבא rejects the רבנן's split of the verses. This closes the back-and-forth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא does not read משרת as teaching a separate rule of טעם כעיקר. For him, both נזיר and חטאת teach the same rule, היתר מצטרף לאיסור. That makes them two verses teaching one idea, so the rule stays limited to those two cases. This brings us back to his position in step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: Both of them
And so they become
They do not teach (a general rule)

steps.whatToRemember: The disagreement is about how to read the verses. The רבנן say נזיר and חטאת teach different rules, so a general rule follows. רבי עקיבא says they teach the same rule, so it stays limited to נזיר and חטאת.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: תַּרְוַיְיהוּ לְהֶיתֵּר מִצְטָרֵף לְאִיסּוּר,
phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva: both of them teach that permitted joins with forbidden,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָווּ לְהוּ שְׁנֵי כְתוּבִין הַבָּאִין כְּאֶחָד,
phrases.english: and so they are two verses that come as one,
and any two verses that come as one
do not teach (a general rule).

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: תַּרְוַיְיהוּ לְהֶיתֵּר מִצְטָרֵף לְאִיסּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the רבנן's reading in step 8
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The רבנן's claim that משרת teaches a separate rule of טעם כעיקר
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Both verses actually teach the same rule, היתר מצטרף לאיסור, so they are שני כתובים הבאין כאחד
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For רבי עקיבא, היתר מצטרף לאיסור is limited to נזיר and חטאת and cannot be applied to the whole Torah.

steps.title: רב אשי asks why a verse is needed for two forbidden foods combining
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי quotes a ברייתא. It learns from a verse that the different forbidden grape products of a נזיר combine. He asks why this verse is needed according to רבי עקיבא. If even forbidden and permitted foods combine, then surely two forbidden foods combine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to רב כהנא: But what about this ברייתא? It says the verse 'of all that is made of the grapevine, from the חרצנים to the זג' teaches that a נזיר's forbidden foods combine with each other. Now think about it. According to רבי עקיבא, forbidden and permitted foods combine. Do we really need a verse to tell us that forbidden and forbidden combine?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי challenges רבי עקיבא's view from a ברייתא. The ברייתא uses a verse for something that should be obvious according to רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי עקיבא, permitted food can 'join' forbidden food to reach the punishable amount. That is the bigger חידוש. It should then be obvious that two forbidden foods join together. So why would the Torah need a separate verse to teach that the נזיר's forbidden foods combine?

keyTerms.meaning: The forbidden foods of a נזיר (grape products such as wine, grapes, seeds and skins)
One part of the grape (seeds or skins; the תנאים argue which is which)
The other part of the grape (skins or seeds)
Combine, join together to reach the minimum amount for punishment
Is it necessary? (a rhetorical 'surely this is obvious')

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְרַב כָּהֲנָא,
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to Rav Kahana:
But what about that which is taught in a baraita:
"Of anything that is made of the grapevine,
from the chartzanim to the zag" (grape seeds and skins)
this taught about the prohibitions of a nazir
that they combine with one another.
Now: according to Rabbi Akiva,
forbidden and permitted foods combine;
is it necessary to teach that forbidden and forbidden combine?!
phrases.notes: This should be obvious, so the פסוק looks extra.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְרַב כָּהֲנָא, אֶלָּא הָא דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 9, where רבי עקיבא holds היתר מצטרף לאיסור. It now asks why another verse would be needed for a case that should be even more obvious.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's position that היתר מצטרף לאיסור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קל וחומר logic. If permitted food combines with forbidden food, then forbidden food surely combines with forbidden food. So the ברייתא's verse for אִיסּוּר וְאִיסּוּר seems unnecessary.

steps.title: רב כהנא explains the two kinds of combining are different
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא answers that the verse is needed. Forbidden plus permitted combine only when eaten at the same time. Two forbidden foods combine even when eaten one after the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Forbidden and permitted combine only when eaten together at once. Forbidden and forbidden combine even when eaten one after the other.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא answers רב אשי's question. He shows that the נזיר verse teaches something new that רבי עקיבא's rule does not cover.
steps.deeperAnalysis: היתר מצטרף לאיסור works only when the permitted and forbidden food are eaten together, like in one mixture. The נזיר verse teaches more. Two forbidden foods add up even when eaten separately, for example half a כזית of seeds and then half a כזית of skins. So the verse is not extra.

keyTerms.meaning: At one time, together (eaten at once)
One after the other (eaten separately, in sequence)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי עקיבא there are two levels of combining. Permitted food joins forbidden food only when eaten together. Two forbidden foods join even when eaten one after the other.

phrases.english: He said to him:
forbidden and permitted combine only at one time (eaten together);
forbidden and forbidden combine even one after the other.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִיסּוּר וְהֶיתֵּר בְּבַת אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the קשיא of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction (חילוק) between two kinds of combining
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since forbidden plus permitted combine, forbidden plus forbidden must obviously combine, so the verse is extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: Forbidden plus permitted combine only when eaten at once. The verse teaches that two forbidden foods combine even when eaten one after another, which is a new rule.

steps.title: משנה: dough stuck in the cracks of a kneading bowl before Pesach
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that dough stuck in the cracks of a kneading bowl must be removed if there is a כזית in one spot. If there is less, it is nullified because it is so small.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Dough that is in the cracks of a kneading bowl: if there is a כזית in one place, one must remove it. If not, it is בטל because it is so small.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It tells us when leftover dough stuck in a bowl's cracks counts as חמץ that must be removed before פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key number is a כזית gathered in one spot. Many tiny scattered bits do not add up to a כזית. Less than a כזית in one place is treated as unimportant and becomes בטל to the bowl, so one does not need to dig it out.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (marks the start of a new משנה)
The cracks of a kneading bowl
An olive-bulk, the basic minimum amount in many הלכות
To remove or destroy (the חמץ)
Nullified because of its small amount

steps.confusionAlert: The word (לֹא) is in parentheses in the printed text. It means 'and if there is not a כזית in one place.' The משנה's plain wording requires a כזית in ONE place. Whether separate smaller pieces can ever combine is not settled by this line. The גמרא takes up that question on the next amud.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: Dough that is in the cracks of a kneading bowl:
if there is an olive-bulk in one place,
one is obligated to remove it;
and if not,
it is nullified because of its small amount.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the previous discussion and opens a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כזית of dough in one spot in the bowl's cracks must be removed. Less than that is בטל.

steps.title: משנה: whether the dough in the cracks blocks immersion of the bowl
steps.stepSummary: The משנה applies the same idea to טומאה. When the bowl is immersed, dough the owner cares about removing is a חציצה. Dough he wants to keep there counts as part of the bowl.
steps.simpleTranslation: And similarly regarding טומאה: if he is particular about the dough, it is a חציצה. If he wants it to stay, it is like the bowl itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a second ruling about the same stuck dough. This time the question is about immersing the bowl in a מקוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a vessel is immersed, nothing may block the water from touching it. The test is the owner's attitude. If he is bothered by the dough and plans to remove it, it is a separate thing and it blocks. If he is happy for it to stay, for example to seal the crack, it becomes part of the bowl and does not block.

keyTerms.meaning: Ritual impurity (here, purifying the bowl by immersion)
Particular about it, bothered by it and wants it removed
Interposes, blocks the water from reaching the vessel
Wants it to remain in place

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic source for a key rule of חציצה: whether something counts as a blockage depends on whether the owner is מקפיד on it.

phrases.english: And similarly, regarding ritual impurity:
if he is particular about it, it interposes;
and if he wants it to remain,
it is like the kneading bowl itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה. It moves from the חמץ question to the טומאה question about the same dough.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dough in the cracks is a חציצה for the bowl's טבילה if the owner is מקפיד on it. If he wants it to stay, it counts as part of the bowl.

steps.title: First version: dough that strengthens the bowl need not be removed
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל on the רישא of the משנה. The duty to remove a כזית applies only where the dough does not strengthen the bowl.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: The משנה only taught that you must remove the dough in a place where it does not strengthen the bowl. But where it does strengthen the bowl, you do not have to remove it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts by limiting the משנה's rule that a כזית of dough in one spot must be removed. שמואל says this applies only when the dough does not serve to strengthen the bowl.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some dough sits in a crack and plugs or reinforces the bowl, so the owner wants it there. שמואל says that kind of dough counts as part of the bowl, so even a full כזית does not have to be removed. The משנה's 'must remove' covers only dough that is just sitting in the crack doing nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this when… (a phrase that limits a rule to a specific case)
To strengthen or reinforce (here, the dough plugs and supports the bowl)
To remove or destroy the חמץ
An olive's volume, the minimum amount that matters here

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
They taught this only
in a place where the pieces do not serve to strengthen the bowl,
phrases.notes: This refers to the רישא of the משנה: a כזית in one place must be removed.

phrases.english: but in a place where they serve to strengthen it —
he is not obligated to remove it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה quoted in steps 12–13 and adds a condition to its רישא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כזית of dough must be removed only if it does not strengthen the bowl. If it strengthens the bowl, it need not be removed.

steps.title: Inference from the first version: less than a כזית never needs removal
steps.stepSummary: From the first version we learn that less than a כזית does not need to be removed, even where it does not strengthen the bowl.
steps.simpleTranslation: We can learn from this that less than a כזית does not have to be removed, even in a place where it does not strengthen the bowl.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a logical conclusion from שמואל's first version about the smaller case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל made strengthening matter only for a full כזית. So for less than a כזית, the plain סיפא of the משנה stays as it is: it is nullified because it is so small. The location does not matter in that case.

keyTerms.meaning: By implication; we can infer
Less than an olive's volume

phrases.english: This implies that less than an olive-bulk —
even in a place where it does not serve to strengthen the bowl
he is not obligated to remove it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the logical result of step 14 for the less-than-כזית case.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to the first version, less than a כזית is always nullified, whatever its location. Only a כזית in a non-strengthening place must be removed.

steps.title: Second version: שמואל's statement is on the סיפא
steps.stepSummary: Others place שמואל's statement on the סיפא. Less than a כזית is nullified only where it strengthens the bowl. Otherwise it must be removed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some teach this statement on the end of the משנה: 'And if not, it is nullified because it is so small.' רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: This was taught only in a place where the dough strengthens the bowl. But in a place where it does not strengthen the bowl, you must remove it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of שמואל's statement. In this version, the condition about strengthening the bowl is attached to the small-amount case instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the 'nullified because it is so small' rule needs two things: less than a כזית, and the dough must strengthen the bowl. Small dough that is just sitting in a crack must still be removed. So this version is stricter than the first.

keyTerms.meaning: Some teach it (introduces an alternate version)
The latter clause of the משנה
Nullified because of its small size

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix the two versions. The first version is lenient on a strengthening כזית and on small dough anywhere. The second version is strict on both of those cases. The two versions agree on only two cases: a non-strengthening כזית must be removed, and strengthening dough smaller than a כזית need not be.

phrases.english: Some teach it on the latter clause:
'And if not, it is nullified due to its small amount.'
Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בִּמְקוֹם הֶעָשׂוּי לְחַזֵּק,
phrases.english: They taught this only in a place where it serves to strengthen the bowl,
but in a place where it does not serve to strengthen it —
he is obligated to remove it,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a competing version of step 14, attaching שמואל's condition to the סיפא instead of the רישא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Less than a כזית is nullified only if it strengthens the bowl. If it does not strengthen the bowl, it must be removed.

steps.title: Inference from the second version: a כזית always needs removal
steps.stepSummary: From the second version we learn that a כזית must be removed, even where it strengthens the bowl.
steps.simpleTranslation: We can learn from this that a כזית must be removed, even in a place where it strengthens the bowl.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the logical conclusion of the second version for the full-כזית case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, strengthening the bowl helps only small dough. A full כזית falls under the רישא without any condition, so it must always be removed. This is the exact opposite of the first version's result for a strengthening כזית.

keyTerms.meaning: That an olive's volume (of dough)
Obligated
Even

steps.whatToRemember: Version 1: strengthening dough of any size, and small dough anywhere, may stay. Version 2: only small dough that strengthens the bowl may stay. Everything else must be removed.

phrases.english: This implies that an olive-bulk —
even in a place where it serves to strengthen the bowl
he is obligated to remove it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the logical result of step 16 for the full-כזית case, the mirror image of step 15.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to the second version, a כזית must always be removed, even if it strengthens the bowl.

steps.title: Each version has a supporting ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces that one ברייתא supports the first version and another supports the second version.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught that matches the first version, and a ברייתא was taught that matches the second version.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא tells us both versions have backing from a ברייתא, and it is about to quote them one at a time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא is not choosing a winner here. It shows that each version matches an older teaching, so both are well grounded. The next steps bring the actual texts.

keyTerms.meaning: The first version
The latter (second) version

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita in accordance with the first version,
and it was taught in a baraita in accordance with the latter version.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּלִישָּׁנָא קַמָּא, תַּנְיָא כְּלִישָּׁנָא בָּתְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces outside support for both versions laid out in steps 14–17.

steps.title: The ברייתא for the first version: the location rule
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules that dough strengthening the bowl is not a חציצה and is not a violation of owning חמץ. Dough not strengthening the bowl is both.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught according to the first version: Dough in the cracks of a kneading bowl, in a place where it strengthens the bowl, is not a barrier for טבילה, and you do not transgress by owning it. In a place where it does not strengthen the bowl, it is a barrier, and you do transgress.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts quoting the ברייתא that supports the first version. This part sets out the basic rule that depends on whether the dough strengthens the bowl.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא ties together both topics of the משנה: טבילה (חציצה) and פסח (בל יראה). Dough that strengthens the bowl counts as part of the bowl, so it is neither a barrier nor forbidden חמץ. At this point the ברייתא has not yet said what size it is talking about. That comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Dough
The cracks of a kneading bowl
Forms a barrier that blocks the water of a טבילה
Transgresses (the ban on owning חמץ on פסח)

phrases.english: It was taught in accordance with the first version:
Dough that is in the cracks of a kneading bowl,
in a place where it serves to strengthen the bowl —
it does not interpose, and one does not transgress.
And in a place where it does not serve to strengthen it —
it interposes, and one transgresses.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּלִישָּׁנָא קַמָּא: בָּצֵק שֶׁבְּסִידְקֵי עֲרֵיבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins quoting the first ברייתא announced in step 18.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא about dough in the cracks of a kneading bowl

steps.title: The ברייתא limits the location rule to a כזית
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא clarifies that the location rule applies to a כזית. Less than a כזית is never a barrier and never a violation, even where it does not strengthen the bowl.
steps.simpleTranslation: When does this apply? With a כזית. But with less than a כזית, even in a place where it does not strengthen the bowl, it is not a barrier, and you do not transgress.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes by saying what size it was talking about. This detail is what proves the first version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the location rule is about a כזית, a strengthening כזית does not need removal. That matches step 14. And less than a כזית is fine even in a non-strengthening place, which matches step 15. Both points contradict the second version.

keyTerms.meaning: When does this statement apply? (introduces a limit)
With an olive's volume
But

steps.whatToRemember: This ברייתא matches the first version exactly. A strengthening כזית may stay, and less than a כזית may stay anywhere.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the first version is not just a reading of the משנה. It is directly stated in an older ברייתא, for both חציצה and חמץ.

phrases.english: In what case is this said?
With an olive-bulk,
but with less than an olive-bulk —
even in a place where it does not serve to strengthen the bowl,
it does not interpose, and one does not transgress.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא from step 19 with the size limit that proves the first version.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's first version and its inference (steps 14–15)
steps.raayaSupportSource: The closing clause of the ברייתא: 'בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים בִּכְזַיִת'

steps.title: A second ברייתא begins, matching the second version
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts quoting a ברייתא that supports the second version of שמואל's statement. It opens with dough in the cracks of a kneading bowl, in a place where the dough strengthens the bowl.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a ברייתא was taught that matches the second version: dough that is in the cracks of a kneading bowl, in a place where it serves to strengthen the bowl —
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is now quoting the second ברייתא it promised, the one that fits the second version of שמואל's statement. This line only sets up the case. The rulings come in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the second version, less than a כזית is nullified only where it strengthens the bowl, and a full כזית must always be removed. This ברייתא begins with the same case of dough that strengthens the bowl. Watch for how it treats the size of the dough, because that is where it will match the second version.

keyTerms.meaning: The latter version, meaning the second way of reporting שמואל's statement
Cracks, splits
A kneading bowl or trough for dough
That serves to strengthen, meaning the dough helps seal and hold the bowl together

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a complete ruling. The dash at the end means the ברייתא continues. Do not try to draw a conclusion until you see its rulings on the next amud.

phrases.english: And it was taught in accordance with the latter version:
phrases.notes: Here comes a second ברייתא, the one that fits the second version of what שמואל said.

phrases.english: Dough that is in the cracks of a kneading bowl,
phrases.notes: Same basic case as the earlier ברייתא

phrases.english: in a place where it serves to strengthen —
phrases.notes: The dough helps the bowl hold together. The ruling follows on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 18 announced two supporting ברייתות. Steps 19-20 gave the first one. This step begins the second one, which supports the second version from Steps 16-17.
steps.raayaObject: The second version of שמואל's statement: less than a כזית is nullified only where it strengthens the bowl, and a כזית must be removed even where it strengthens the bowl.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about dough in the cracks of a kneading bowl. Its opening case is quoted here, and its rulings continue on the next amud.
